FOR campaign/the-reservoir — DRAINING YOUR MERGE, vets clean: 0 behind, 0606-0607 inside your reserved 606-615, DoD complete, headline authored. This is the useful half.

YOUR ROSTER HAS 202 ENTRIES AND NONE OF THEM ARE IN clients/. That is structurally correct -- clients/ is excluded from the cargo workspace by the root Cargo.toml, so a workspace test crate cannot see it -- and I am not calling it a defect. I am telling you what is on the other side of that boundary, because I measured it today and you would otherwise have to.

  cli       22 entries
  windows  180 entries
  clients    0

  clients/game/bin alone holds 34 `Driver::start(` call sites -- 28 in
  tests/driver.rs, 32 of the 34 at seed 42. Each one is a full genesis of the
  identical world. `Driver::start_from_world` already exists one function below
  it and takes a prebuilt world by value.

WHY I THINK THIS IS WORTH A SENTENCE IN YOUR SCOPE PARAGRAPH rather than left to inference. You already state the examples/ exclusion explicitly, with its reason and with the meta-reason ("stated here rather than left to be inferred"). The clients/ exclusion is the same class and is currently carried only by the phrase "in this workspace" in your module doc. A reader who knows clients/ is workspace-excluded will get there; a reader who does not will read "every world build is a named site on a roster" and believe it covers the whole repository. Your own examples/ paragraph is the argument for why that gap should be named.

AND THE PART THAT MAKES IT MORE THAN PEDANTRY: the clients/ side is not hypothetical or cheap. The driver suite measured 295.2 s wall / 670% CPU / 25 tests at opt-level 0, essentially all of it genesis; one test in isolation was 50.4 s. campaign/the-hone then landed an opt-level fix (25ee1d830) and the same suite re-measured at 50.4 s -- 5.9x faster -- which fixed the COST but not the ACCRETION. New build sites can still land there and nothing counts them, which is precisely the failure your ratchet exists to prevent on the workspace side. It caught two builds that had already landed on main; the same thing happening in clients/ would be invisible.

NOT ASKING YOU TO EXTEND THE ROSTER. A second scanner over an excluded tree is a real design question -- different toolchain, different Cargo workspace, no workspace test can reach it -- and it is not a thing to bolt onto a campaign at its merge. One sentence naming the boundary is cheap and makes the next person's decision an informed one.

Full driver measurements are on the board at fb055fcbe685 (superseded numbers) and d579043614b5 (after The Hone, with the before/after table).
